Unauthorized Access to Admin Interface [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-284] on Cognito User Pools, API Gateway, Lambda Functions, ECS Containers: Without proper role-based access control (RBAC) and IAM policies, administrative interfaces could be accessed by regular users or attackers who obtain valid credentials. An attacker with valid user credentials attempts to access admin endpoints by manipulating API requests, potentially gaining elevated privileges.

API Rate Limiting Bypass [Denial of Service, CWE-770] on API Gateway, Lambda Functions, ECS Containers, RDS Instance, DynamoDB Table: Without rate limiting, attackers can flood the API with requests, potentially exhausting resources or causing service degradation. An attacker scripts multiple concurrent requests to API endpoints, causing increased latency or failures for legitimate users.

Container Scaling Security Issues [Denial of Service, Information Disclosure, CWE-670] on ECS Containers, Application Load Balancer: Improper scaling configurations can lead to container termination without proper connection draining, causing service disruptions. During high load, rapid scaling events could cause connection drops or expose container metadata to attackers.

Analytics Pipeline Data Access Control Issues [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-306] on Kinesis Data Streams, Glue ETL, Redshift, QuickSight: Lack of fine-grained access controls and data filtering in the analytics pipeline could expose sensitive data to unauthorized users. An analyst with QuickSight access could view sensitive customer data that should be restricted or anonymized.

TLS Configuration Vulnerabilities [Tampering, Information Disclosure, CWE-295] on CloudFront, API Gateway, Application Load Balancer: Without proper TLS configuration, communication between clients and services could be intercepted or modified. An attacker performs a man-in-the-middle attack on unencrypted or improperly encrypted communications.

DNS-Level Attacks [Spoofing, Tampering, CWE-350] on CloudFront, API Gateway: Without proper DNS protection, attackers could hijack DNS requests or perform DNS poisoning attacks. An attacker attempts to redirect traffic by manipulating DNS responses or performing DNS cache poisoning.

Insecure Direct Object References in API [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-639] on API Gateway, Lambda Functions, DynamoDB Table, RDS Instance: APIs might use predictable resource IDs or fail to verify access permissions before returning data. An attacker modifies resource IDs in API requests to access unauthorized data.

Insufficient Logging and Monitoring [Repudiation, CWE-778] on All Components: Without proper logging and monitoring, security incidents might not be detected or investigated effectively. An attacker performs reconnaissance or data exfiltration without detection due to insufficient logging.
